title: Concurrency & race conditions
hook: Two threads can both read a value, both add one, and both write — and you lose an update.

steps.caption: Both threads read count as 0 before either writes back.
A writes 1, then B writes 1 — second write wins. One increment vanished.

nodeCaptions.mem: Final value 1, not 2. Timing decided correctness.
nodeCaptions.t2: Locks, atomics, or queues prevent this interleaving.

takeaways: A race is when result depends on unpredictable timing of shared access.
Read-modify-write without synchronization is a classic bug pattern.
Fix with mutual exclusion or lock-free atomics designed for the job.

quiz.question: In the lost-update race, why did count stay 1 after two increments?
choices: Addition is illegal on shared memory
Both threads based their write on the same old read
The CPU rejects the second write always
quiz.explanation: Both computed 0+1; the later write overwrote the earlier one.
